The document correctly asserts that AI depends on foundational  data infrastructure but doesn’t define a structured multi-layered framework or roadmap to guide its adoption.
Countries would benefit from a blueprint of sorts for them to understand the critical investments (e.g., compute infrastructure, data governance, applications, etc) and how to go about setting them up.
A defined/custom AI capability stack guide in understanding how DPI-H relate to AI infrastructure

The document correctly asserts that AI depends on foundational  data infrastructure but doesn’t define a structured multi-layered framework or roadmap to guide its adoption.
Countries would benefit from a blueprint of sorts for them to understand the critical investments (e.g., compute infrastructure, data governance, applications, etc) and how to go about setting them up.
A defined/custom AI capability stack guide in understanding how DPI-H relate to AI infrastructure
public.suggestedRevision:
Consider adding a new sub-section in Chapter 5 that defines an AI capabilty framework with layers: 
(1) Data foundations (DPI-H components like registries, LHR, LIMR, TS) that provide governed, structured data
(2) Interoperability and access  (exchange layer that allows data to flow to models) 
(3) Model development and inference (infrastructure for training, testing, and deploying models)
(4) Governance and oversight (policies and processes for trustworthy AI) 
(5) AI-enabled applications (point-of-care and analytical tools that consume AI outputs). 

Also include an indicative implementation sequence: countries should establish layers 1–2 before meaningful AI adoption.
